metrics.label: Precision (set)
metrics.description: Fraction of the whole returned list that is relevant. A set measure, not P@k — its value moves with the run length, which is why top_k is reported beside it.

metrics.label: Recall (set)
metrics.description: Fraction of the relevant documents that were retrieved. Pooled recall: the denominator counts only judged relevant documents.

metrics.label: F₁
metrics.description: Harmonic mean of precision and recall.

metrics.label: Average precision
metrics.description: Mean of the precisions observed at each relevant document, divided by the number of relevant documents in the judgments. Averaged over queries this is MAP, the primary metric — the appendix cites Buckley & Voorhees for its stability against assessor disagreement.

metrics.label: P@5
metrics.description: Precision among the top 5. Denominator is always 5.

metrics.label: P@10
metrics.description: Precision among the top 10 — what a user sees on one page.

metrics.label: R-Precision
metrics.description: Precision at rank R, where R is the number of relevant documents. Comparable across queries with different R, which P@k is not.

metrics.label: 11-point interpolated PR (TREC)
metrics.description: Interpolated precision at eleven standard recall levels. A query that never reaches a level contributes zero to that level's average.

metrics.label: 11-point interpolated PR (non-zeroing)
metrics.description: ROMIP lists a second, 'RIRES-modified' 11-point curve as official but never defines it in any edition. This is a documented reconstruction: identical to the TREC method except that unreached recall levels are omitted rather than scored zero. Plotted against the TREC curve it shows exactly what the zeroing convention does.

metrics.label: bpref
metrics.description: Binary preference. Skips unjudged documents instead of counting them against the run, so it is the robust measure when the judgment pool does not cover a ranker. Uses trec_eval's min(N, R) denominator.

metrics.label: MRR
metrics.description: Reciprocal rank of the first relevant document.

metrics.label: nDCG@5
metrics.description: Normalised discounted cumulative gain with ROMIP's 2^g − 1 gain.

metrics.label: nDCG@10
metrics.description: Normalised DCG over the top 10.

metrics.label: ERR
metrics.description: Expected reciprocal rank — a cascade model where a document's value is discounted by the chance the user was still looking.

metrics.label: pFound
metrics.description: Yandex/ROMIP cascade metric with an explicit abandonment term.

metrics.label: Retrieved
metrics.description: Documents returned for this query.

metrics.label: Relevant retrieved
metrics.description: Relevant documents found.

metrics.label: Unjudged retrieved
metrics.description: Returned documents carrying no judgment. A high value means the pool does not cover this ranker, and that its scores are pessimistic.

metrics.label: R
metrics.description: Relevant documents in the judgments for this query.

metrics.label: P@1
metrics.description: Precision among the top 1.

metrics.label: P@20
metrics.description: Precision among the top 20.
